title: Ethiopia Mobilizes Global Partnerships, Climate Finance Ahead of COP32
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia is intensifying efforts to build international confidence in its climate commitments, attract climate finance and forge strategic partnerships as it prepares to host the 32nd United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP32) in Addis Ababa in November 2027, Finance Minister and COP32 Chief Negotiator, Fitsum Assefa (PhD) said.

title: Proxy Politics and Border Clashes - an Escalating Crisis Between Sudan and Ethiopia
summary: [Ayin Network] The diplomatic rift between Sudan and Ethiopia has evolved past border disputes this month, exposing competing geopolitical interests along the Red Sea. Last week, Ethiopian authorities shuttered the Sudanese consulate in Assosa, giving staff 48 hours to evacuate. Khartoum swiftly retaliated, closing the Ethiopian consulate in the eastern city of Gedaref and expelling its diplomatic personnel.

title: Families Who Fled Ethiopia for Kenya's Moyale Need Food, Water and Shelter
summary: [UN News] The International Organization of Migration (IOM) and partners are calling for urgent funding to support tens of thousands of people who have escaped violent clashes in Ethiopia for the Moyale region in northern Kenya.

title: Model Citizens - 23 African-Born Immigrant Win in U.S. Elections
summary: [CFR] The growing political visibility of recent African immigrants in the United States is a standing reproach to dated conceptions of belonging back home.

title: Ethiopia Advances COP32 Preparations As COP31 Opens Amid Climate Finance Disputes
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia is using its participation in the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), which opened on Monday in Antalya, Türkiye, to advance preparations for hosting COP32 in Addis Abeba in November 2027, as developing countries push for stronger climate finance commitments amid widening disagreements over how to address the climate crisis.

title: More Than 65 Killed in Armed Attack in Benishangul-Gumuz's Assosa Zone, Residents Say
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- More than 65 people, including members of regional security forces and at least 27 civilians, were killed in a heavily armed attack in Dalati locality of Buldiglu Woreda, Assosa Zone, Benishangul-Gumuz Regional State, residents told Addis Standard.

title: Food Crisis Hits Ethiopians Fleeing Violence Into Kenya's Moyale
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Thousands of Ethiopian families who fled violent clashes in their country and sought refuge in Kenya's Moyale area are facing acute food shortages, with more than seven in ten households reporting insufficient food, a new humanitarian assessment has found.

title: Ethiopia Pavilion Officially Opens At COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The Ethiopia Pavilion officially opened today at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, showcasing the nation's climate leadership and green transformation to the global community.

title: Ethiopia Advances COP32 Preparations As President-Designate Arrives in Türkiye
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- COP32 President-Designate Gedion Timothewos (PhD) has arrived in Antalya, Türkiye, to participate in the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31).

title: Political Parties Must Lead Africa's Economic Transformation - Pan-African Parliament President
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- African political parties must play a greater role in driving economic transformation and strengthening the continent's sovereignty and institutions, Said President of the Pan-African Parliament, Dr. Fateh Boutbig.

title: Egypt's Conspiracy Against Ethiopia Over Abay River, Red Sea No Longer Workable, Says Water Minister
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Egypt's longstanding diplomatic and political conspiracy to block Ethiopia's development projects on Abay River and isolate the country from the Red Sea are no longer effective, Water and Energy Minister Habtamu Itefa said.

title: AU Commission Chief Urges Parties to Focus On Serving Citizens and Strengthening Nat'l Interests
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Political parties must go beyond seeking power and focus on serving citizens, strengthening democratic governance and building consensus on Africa's development priorities, African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf said today.

title: Ethiopia, France Vow to Deepen Military and Strategic Cooperation
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia and France have pledged to deepen their longstanding military and strategic cooperation, with renewed emphasis on military capacity building, knowledge transfer and regional peace and stability.

title: PM Abiy Urges African Political Parties to Prioritize Leadership Renewal, Long-Term Dev't
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed called on African political parties to embrace leadership renewal and build consensus on long-term national priorities.

title: UN Report Says UAE Firm Hired Colombian Mercenaries to Fight in Sudan, Raising Questions Over Abu Dhabi's UN Chief Bid
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba- A confidential UN report reportedly details how an Abu Dhabi-based security company with links to the Emirati ruling family recruited and deployed hundreds of Colombian former military personnel to fight alongside Sudan's Rapid Support Forces, intensifying questions over the UAE's nomination of diplomat Lana Nusseibeh to lead the United Nations.

title: AI, Terrorism Top AU-EU Security Talks in Addis Ababa
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The African Union (AU) and European Union (EU) are seeking to strengthen coordinated responses to Africa's evolving security challenges, with maritime insecurity, terrorism and the growing influence of artificial intelligence emerging as key priorities for cooperation.

title: IG Kanja Orders Additional Police Deployment to Moyale Amid Ethiopia Border Crisis
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered the deployment of additional police officers to Moyale, Marsabit County, amid growing security concerns over escalating violence in neighbouring Ethiopia that has forced thousands of people to flee across the border into Kenya.

title: African Political Parties Summit Delegates Witness Addis Ababa's Urban Transformation
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- African Political Parties Summit delegates have toured Addis Ababa's major urban development projects, witnessing the Ethiopian capital's ongoing transformation into a modern, inclusive and more accessible city.

title: Ethiopia Suspends the Reporter Indefinitely in Escalating Assault On Independent Media
summary: [CPJ] Nairobi -- The Committee to Protect Journalists calls on Ethiopian authorities to immediately lift the indefinite suspension of The Reporter, one of the country's oldest independent newspapers.

title: Germany Cautions 'Any Escalation in the Horn of Africa Must Be Avoided'
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Germany's Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has warned that "any escalation in the Horn of Africa must be avoided," as Ethiopia's relations with neighboring Eritrea and Sudan deteriorate, reaffirming Berlin's support for stability in northern Ethiopia.

title: Winning Wars, Losing Peace - Ethiopia's Unfinished Political Struggle for Lasting Stability
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- In contrast to 2018, when Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed took office, many Ethiopians hoped the country was entering a new era of peace and development; unfortunately, today, Ethiopia faces a dangerous convergence of armed conflicts, expanding battlefronts, unresolved territorial disputes, competing political ambitions, and regional tensions. Together, these crises threaten national stability and the lives, livelihoods, and future of millions.

summary: [Daba Finance] Ethiopia has become Africa's fifth-largest economy after revising its gross domestic product figures to account for sectors including digital finance, services and manufacturing. The country's economy was valued at $210.7 billion in the fiscal year ended July 2026, Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa announced on November 4. title: Ethiopia Puts Youth At Center of Governance, Leadership - Minister
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has placed youth empowerment and participation at the center of its governance and development agenda, with young people holding more than 50 percent of leadership positions at the federal level, Minister of Youth and Sports Aklilu Tadesse said.

title: African Parties Gather in Addis to Discuss Governing for Growth
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Political party leaders, Heads of State, and policymakers from across the continent have gathered in Addis Ababa today, November 5, 2026, for the Second African Political Parties Summit (APPS) to deliberate on strategies for steering employment creation, inclusive development, and the structural transformation of African economies.

title: M-Pesa, Ethiopia Operations Push Safaricom Half-Year Profit to Sh58.2bn
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Safaricom's net profit rose by 35.9 percent to Sh58.2 billion in the six months to September, helped by higher M-Pesa revenue and growth in its Ethiopia business.
